captions: Figure S1: Example of a diffraction pattern collected at 63.7 GPa and 1480 K, analyzed using GSAS software and its graphical interface EXPGUI (Toby, 2001). At these P-T conditions the FeS sample adopts a MnP-type structure (FeS-VI) and the KCl pressure medium adopts a B2 structure. A minor contribution from FeS2 is also observed.
Figure S2: Integrated XRD patterns at four different pressures with increasing temperature (see Table S2). The appearance of diffuse scattering is used to determine the onset of melting.

Figure S3 : Volume of FeS at different pressures and temperatures, fitted to a MnP structure. The absence of volume discontinuities with increasing temperature across the structural changes between FeS-VI (red squares), FeS-IV (green hexagons) and FeS-IX (blue dots) indicates that the phase transitions are second order.

Figure S4 : Diffraction patterns at different temperatures illustrating the structural evolution from FeS VI to FeS IV and to FeS IX at the three selected pressures, as in Figure 3. The analysis is performed using GSAS software and its graphical interface EXPGUI (Toby, 2001).
Figure S5: Difference between observed pressures and calculated pressures according to the thermal EoS determined in this study.

figure_s5.visual_bound_exceedances: Points visually reach approximately +3.6 and -3.2 GPa; not a digitized numerical table.
figure_s5.qualification: The supplied input files and saved EOS have not been shown to reproduce this raster plot. Cold point pressures overlap the additional 300 K observations in the 178-row file, but that does not identify the plot model or row mask.
